findings.title: Read-only group permission authorizes group creation
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-Groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses this check to authorize POST /groups, so an administrator granted only read access can create groups or move existing subgroups to the top level. This check must require MANAGE rather than VIEW; add a negative test for a view-only all-Groups permission.

findings.title: Authorization resource IDs are used as group IDs
findings.body: groupResource.getId() is the authorization resource's generated ID, not the GroupModel ID stored in its name. Passing it to hasPermission() therefore looks up the wrong name, and adding it to granted supplies invalid IDs to user membership queries. In particular, a view-members or manage-members grant on all Groups returns the aggregate authorization resource's UUID; UsersResource then filters by that UUID and returns no users, and /users/count is also incorrect. Collect actual group IDs and handle the aggregate Groups resource separately.

findings.title: V2 group managers cannot create group members
findings.body: The group-member creation fallback still checks only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, the V1 feature flag. With V2 enabled, an administrator granted the new manage-members and manage-membership scopes on a group receives 403 from POST /users even when the representation assigns the new user only to that authorized group: canCreateGroupMembers() exits before evaluating those permissions. Allow this fallback for V2 as well and cover group-scoped user creation in the new tests.
